title: The Deepest Point On Earth Is Darker Than You Think
description:
Challenger Deep, at the bottom of the Mariana Trench, is deep enough to swallow Mount Everest with room to spare. This is what it actually takes to survive down there.

#shorts #sciencefacts #ocean

scenes.text: Sunlight stops reaching the ocean in any meaningful way at around one thousand meters down.
The Mariana Trench's deepest point, Challenger Deep, sits almost eleven thousand meters below the surface.
If you dropped Mount Everest into it, the peak would still sit over two kilometers underwater.
Down there, the water pressure is over a thousand times what you feel at the surface, enough to crush most submarines.
And yet, life still finds a way. Researchers have found shrimp-like creatures and even microbial life at the very bottom.
We've mapped more of the surface of Mars than we have of our own ocean floor.
